items.title: Hal Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: Whether it’s Oliver or Muggsy Spanier or Keppard, Tommy Ladnier, or whatever, it’s always the right thing.

ctx.x: Well good for you. That should be doing what you want.

It is. I really like it because he doesn’t let it get boring. I mean he’ll bring in new tunes to play and drop the ones that he’s played a lot, and he’s so versatile on the cornet, and can play all those different styles and make them fit. Whether it’s Oliver or Muggsy Spanier or Keppard, Tommy Ladnier, or whatever, it’s always the right thing. And that inspires me, when you’ve got a hot front line, you’re not going to just sit there and take up space on the bandstand. You want to make it go.
Gee I wonder if those bands ever do the wagon thing anymore, where they put the band on the wagon and they go out?
